note: Inputs for the deterministic bullwhip metrics. Every series is labelled. The engine computes the metric values; nothing here is a result.

metrics.name: Order amplification ratio
metrics.definition: (1 + growth of intermediary orders) / (1 + growth of end demand) over the same 12 months. Above 1.3 means intermediaries are ordering faster than end demand grows: amplification.
metrics.inputs_note: [DEMODATA] intermediary orders = switchgear-OEM relay orders; end demand = energised data-centre MW. Replace with ABB order intake and Fingrid energisation data.

sources.name: Method: Lee, Padmanabhan, Whang (1997) bullwhip definition; ABB order intake (internal, not connected)

metrics.name: Memory price momentum (second derivative)
metrics.definition: Change in the quarter-on-quarter price increment. Prices rising but the increment shrinking two quarters in a row is the pre-peak pattern.
metrics.inputs_note: 1Q26–4Q26 midpoints from TrendForce press releases (2026-02-02, 2026-03-31, 2026-07-09, 2026-09-30); the 4Q25 value is a [DEMODATA] placeholder.

metrics.name: Double-ordering index (lead time vs distributor inventory)
metrics.definition: Lead times and distributor inventory days rising together means buyers are ordering ahead of need (hoarding). Lead times rising while inventory falls means genuine scarcity.
metrics.inputs_note: [DEMODATA] lead time change is consistent with the 32 -> 52 week MCU series (SIG-008); distributor inventory days change is illustrative. Replace with distributor quarterly reports (Arrow, Avnet) and ECIA data.

metrics.name: DRAM spot-to-contract spread
metrics.definition: Spot premium over contract price. A high premium means urgency; a collapsing premium while lead times are still long means hoarding is ending.
metrics.inputs_note: [DEMODATA] entire series illustrative (same as SIG-015). Replace with DRAMeXchange spot vs contract.

metrics.name: Order push-out and cancellation rate (ABB internal)
metrics.definition: Share of frame-order quantities rescheduled out or cancelled in the last 90 days. The earliest internal sign that intermediaries over-ordered.
metrics.inputs_note: Not connected. Requires ABB SAP sales order change history (VBAP/VBEP schedule line changes).

analog_2021_2023.label: SOURCE+DEMODATA
analog_2021_2023.note: Indexed shape of the 2021-2023 semiconductor cycle for visual comparison only. Anchors: Broadcom lead time 12.2 weeks (Feb 2020) to 22.2 weeks (Apr 2021); SIA 2022 sales USD 573.5 bn with December 2022 down 4.4% MoM; memory corrected first in 2022 and rebounded first in 2023. Intermediate points are illustrative.

sources.name: Wikipedia: 2020-2023 global chip shortage (lead time anchors)
Nomad Semi: State of the Semiconductor Cycle (SIA data)
Roland Berger: Semiconductor shortage, a different kind of (Oct 2022)
